concerns.text: T103 mandates statistical_report.json with 'top-level keys p_values and t_statistics (one entry per outcome)' while claiming 'validity_status matching the output contract', but contracts/output.schema.yaml requires a flat per-comparison object with required keys comparison_name, p_value, p_value_corrected, effect_size, effect_size_ci_lower/upper, significance_status, mdes, adjustment_status, validity_status. The task's mandated structure cannot satisfy the contract it references; either the task or the contract must be reconciled before implementation.

T102 writes final_cleaned_dataset.csv with column 'MMSE' (and T101's mapping table targets 'MMSE'), but contracts/dataset.schema.yaml names the optional field 'mmse_score' (integer 0-30) and sets additionalProperties: false. Files produced per the task will fail contract schema validation; the task must either map to mmse_score or the contract must be amended.

T110 updates 'state/state.yaml' with hashes, but the constitution (Principle V / Data Hygiene) mandates checksums recorded in the project state file 'state/projects/PROJ-524-the-impact-of-nostalgia-on-cognitive-fle.yaml' artifact_hashes map. Writing to a different state file is a constitution violation introduced by the task.

FR-005 flags sensitivity for 'p-values' in 0.04-0.06 without specifying raw vs Bonferroni-corrected; T104 evaluates thresholds on corrected p-values but flags is_sensitive_to_threshold on raw p. The task should state which p-value family the borderline rule applies to (and ideally the spec should too) so the FR-005 check is unambiguous.

Data model names the condition field 'stimulus_condition' while T101/T102 and the dataset contract use 'stimulus_type'. The task's mapping table should explicitly note the reconciliation so the implementer does not produce schema-invalid files against one of the two authoritative documents.
